forwarding.checkIt: To check it works, send an email to {{email}} from another account. It shows up as a new ticket in Unassigned.

gmail.s1: In Gmail, open Settings, then See all settings, then Forwarding and POP/IMAP.
gmail.s2: Choose Add a forwarding address and paste the address above.
gmail.s3: Gmail sends a confirmation email. It arrives in opendesk as a ticket: open it and click the link, or copy the code into Gmail.
gmail.s4: Back in Gmail, select Forward a copy of incoming mail to the new address and save.

workspace.s1: For one mailbox, follow the Gmail steps while signed in as that user.
workspace.s2: For a group or many users, open the Google Admin console, then Apps, Google Workspace, Gmail, Routing.
workspace.s3: Add a routing rule for the address, choose Also deliver to and add the address above as a recipient.
workspace.s4: Save. Changes can take a few minutes to apply.

microsoft.s1: Open the Exchange admin center, then Recipients, Mailboxes, and select the mailbox.
microsoft.s2: Under Mail flow settings, choose Manage email forwarding.
microsoft.s3: Turn on forwarding, paste the address above, and keep Deliver to both on if the mailbox should still get a copy.
microsoft.s4: If outbound forwarding is blocked, allow it in the outbound spam policy, or use an Outlook rule that forwards to the address instead.
